archetype: temporary-to-semi-permanent civilian emergency relief shelter organized for intake, triage, sleeping, sanitation, food distribution, staff control and protected utility service
ground_program: clearly marked public arrival and intake zone connected directly to the site approach without forcing civilians through staff or utility spaces
registration and information desk with short controlled queueing space and visible access to the principal shelter hall
first-aid and triage room adjacent to intake but separable from the main sleeping population for privacy and infection control
large subdivided sleeping hall using believable bed or cot bays with continuous aisles, emergency egress and no sealed sleeping pockets
family or vulnerable-person sleeping area separated from the general hall by lightweight partitions or a distinct room while retaining supervised access
food distribution and simple warming kitchen with dry storage, potable-water access and a service path that does not cross sleeping bays
dining or common area sized as a real shared-use space rather than decorative furniture scattered through circulation routes
male, female and accessible sanitation provisions represented with toilets, wash points and privacy partitions where footprint permits
staff office and records station positioned to supervise intake and the principal shelter circulation spine
secure supply store for blankets, medicine, food and emergency equipment with staff-only access
utility or mechanical room containing the shelter's power, water or heating service representation and reachable from a service-side approach
waste and dirty-service exit separated from public intake and food distribution
covered exterior waiting or overflow zone tied to the entrance without blocking emergency access
terrain feathering and drainage that seat the shelter, service apron and approach into surrounding wasteland rather than placing the complex on a monolithic slab
upper_program: prefer a single-storey relief-shelter mass unless the authoritative footprint requires a second level
where an upper level exists, reserve it for staff rest, records, light storage or additional sleeping space reached by a supported stair and real landing
roof volume may carry vents, compact mechanical equipment, water storage or emergency communications only where structurally supported and accessible for maintenance
no decorative inaccessible mezzanines, floating roof equipment or disconnected upper rooms
circulation: public movement follows an intelligible sequence from arrival to intake, triage as needed, sleeping/common areas, sanitation and exit
staff can reach intake, medical, supply, kitchen and utility spaces without crossing sleeping bays unnecessarily
food and clean-supply movement remains separated from waste removal and dirty-service circulation wherever the footprint permits
every occupied room connects to a continuous player-scale route with adequate doorway width, headroom and destination at both ends
at least two credible emergency egress directions serve the principal sleeping hall when footprint size makes a single exit implausible
exterior service access reaches utility and supply zones without cutting through the civilian arrival queue
damage_constraints: the damaged derivative must remain recognizable as an emergency shelter through surviving intake, sleeping, sanitation and supply organization
favor localized roof leaks, damaged partitions, abandoned cots, depleted supplies, failed utilities and weather intrusion over indiscriminate wall deletion
preserve at least one continuous traversable route through intake, the principal shelter hall and a secondary functional zone
damage sanitation, kitchen and utility systems together with their supporting pipes, walls, fixtures or service routes so functional remnants do not float
allow one localized fire, impact or partial roof-collapse event only where adjacent structure and debris tell the same physical story
do not repeat identical missing-wall or rubble masks across sleeping bays
retain emergency signage, supply organization and civilian-use evidence sufficient to distinguish the site from a generic warehouse or barracks
derive damaged, contaminated or occupied variants only from this immutable clean master

required_manual_checks: the structure reads immediately as a civilian emergency relief shelter rather than a warehouse, prison or military barracks
intake, triage, sleeping, sanitation, food, staff, supply and utility functions are spatially distinct and connected by believable circulation
civilian, staff, clean-supply and dirty-service paths do not create obvious functional contradictions
sleeping aisles, doors, stairs if present and emergency exits remain player-scale usable with continuous headroom
kitchen, sanitation and utility fixtures have credible supporting rooms and service relationships rather than decorative placement
damage remains localized and physically coherent while preserving enough program evidence to infer the shelter's original operation
the building, entrance, service edge and drainage meet surrounding terrain without floating slabs, severe steps or a rectangular artificial platform
